title: pattern
content_html:
pattern

In all the little cracks, what first seems to be damage starts to reveal small patterns. How do we decide that several occurrences belong together, and what do we do with one that almost fits? Pattern can be made by following a rule, noticed in something that has already happened or projected when a few details are all we have. The Library’s work on pattern separation and completion offers one way to pursue the question of what recognition supplies. A fragmented composition can still have an order. Spacing, alignment or clustering can give it structure without a regular grid or repeated unit. all the little cracks · Pattern Separation vs Completion

Reading note. Jung. Jung’s foreword to the I Ching considers the significance an observer finds in a coincidence. In all the little cracks, the appearance of a pattern changes how the speaker reads what first seemed like damage. What would count as finding the same pattern again, and what would count as a different reading of it? Jung’s foreword to the I Ching, collected works vol. 11
